correctness.rationale: For any modulus p^e dividing the coefficient gcd, the exact prime-square coefficient forces e≤k. Padding any p-coprime u by p^a with ak≥e removes both n-powers, and c(p^a)=0 forces the two prime-power divisor sums equal. Multiplicativity then shows sigma_k(u)=sigma_ell(u) modulo p^e; Möbius inversion forces all unit power differences to vanish. Multiples of p vanish since e≤k. This is the needed reverse divisibility; the forward divisibility follows from the exact divisor-sum identity. Carmichael exponents determine all valuations including p=2, p odd and k=1 boundaries. Two distinct computational implementations agree for 60 exponent pairs and 10,740 coefficients, but infinite correctness rests on the written argument.

originality.rationale: The 2024 Craig–van Ittersum–Ono Lemmas 9 and 12 prove prime-detecting and integrality/unit-content claims for different distinguished forms, while the 2025 Kane–Krishnamoorthy–Lau theorem classifies the prime-detecting space by signs. The 2026 Allen–Craig paper analyzes coefficient growth and prime factors; it defines the same two-parameter coefficients but does not give their exact all-index gcd in the inspected text. The new statement is the sharp universal divisibility of this whole two-parameter family, proved via prime-power padding and Möbius inversion. Own historical claim comparison, web query variants, and published findings yield no covering result; unindexed equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: The fixed-divisor formula itself is classical; novelty is only asserted for its equality with the full Fourier-coefficient content in this family.
Unindexed or undetected equivalent treatments of this natural congruence question could exist; unsuccessful searches do not establish uniqueness.
The original paper Lemma 12 has other integral primitive forms, but its statement is not directly a claim about this entire c_{k,ell} family.

value.rationale: The recent Allen–Craig work uses the entire two-parameter positive coefficient family as quantitative arithmetic objects, for prime factors, factorization heuristics, and primes in intervals. The maximal all-coefficient congruence modulus is a natural global invariant of these objects: it determines exactly which divisibility constraints are forced independent of input n and canonically produces primitive integral positive-index coefficient sequences. The result supplies a complete prime-power classification with an informative dependence on the exponent difference, not an isolated small numerical normalization. It is sharp across infinitely many pairs, even when k,l are odd so the series have a genuine quasimodular interpretation, and the reverse fixed-divisor equality has a nontrivial structural proof. It does not assert a downstream factorization or prime-gap advance.
